lean.faithfulness_note: STATEMENT ONLY: the cited theorem of Laurent (1984) on torsion points of subvarieties of the torus is sorry (Mathlib has nothing on it), and count_law_torsion is proved from it. Proved without it: Lemma 1 (q(q-1))^(i-1) S_i = U_i(q,q^c) for all integer words, the equivalence between V_i(k) as points of X_i and Phi_k | S_i, and k-torsion of the points. Torus is over C (not a number field). The set equality 'torsion points of X_i = union y_nu H_nu' is read as Laurent's theorem states it (torsion points of finitely many torsion cosets contained in X_i). NOT expressed: the passage to k-independent congruences (Theorem A displayed formula, beta_s), Theorems B and C (polynomiality and degree).
